avalancheActivity.highlights: Fresh and older wind slabs are to be assessed with care and prudence.
avalancheActivity.comment:
The sometimes strong wind has transported the new snow significantly. Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls the wind slabs have increased in size additionally. Above approximately 2300 m the avalanches can be triggered in the new snow and wind slab layers and reach large size.
New snow and wind slabs can in some cases be released by a single winter sport participant. This applies in particular on very steep slopes at intermediate and high altitudes.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

snowpackStructure.comment: 30 to 40 cm of snow fell in the last few days above approximately 1500 m. The sometimes moderate wind has transported the new snow. Faceted weak layers exist in the snowpack in particular in places that are protected from the wind, especially in the Prealps.

avalancheActivity.highlights: Wind slabs represent the main danger.
avalancheActivity.comment:
The sometimes strong wind has transported the new snow significantly. Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls the wind slabs have increased in size additionally. In particular here medium-sized and, in isolated cases, large avalanches are possible.
In addition the soft wind slabs above the tree line are easily triggered.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

snowpackStructure.comment: 30 to 50 cm of snow fell in the last few days above approximately 1800 m. The sometimes moderate wind has transported the new snow. Faceted weak layers exist in the snowpack in particular in places that are protected from the wind. Below approximately 2000 m from a snow sport perspective, in most cases insufficient snow is lying.

avalancheActivity.highlights: Wind slabs at intermediate and high altitudes. Slab avalanches are possible.
avalancheActivity.comment:
The sometimes strong wind has transported the new snow. In particular adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls small and, in isolated cases, medium-sized slab avalanches are possible. In addition the soft wind slabs are capable of being triggered.
In particular on very steep sunny slopes and in steep rocky terrain small and medium-sized dry and moist avalanches are possible as a consequence of solar radiation.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.

snowpackStructure.comment: 20 to 30 cm of snow fell in the last few days above approximately 1500 m. The wind has transported the new snow significantly. The solar radiation will give rise as the day progresses to moistening of the snowpack in particular at low and intermediate altitudes.

avalancheActivity.highlights: Individual avalanche prone locations are to be found on wind-loaded slopes at intermediate and high altitudes.
avalancheActivity.comment: The avalanche prone locations are very rare. They are to be found on extremely steep shady slopes in high Alpine regions and on wind-loaded slopes. As a consequence of solar radiation individual small natural moist avalanches are possible. Restraint should be exercised because avalanches can sweep people along and give rise to falls. The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.

snowpackStructure.comment: 15 to 30 cm of snow fell in the last few days above approximately 1600 m. The moderate wind has transported some snow. The new snow is loosely bonded on wind-protected shady slopes. As a consequence of solar radiation a crust will form on the surface.
